text.p: Economic activity in Lebanon rose in July to its highest level in more than three-and-a-half years, fuelled by increased construction, the Bank of Lebanon said on Wednesday.
The bank's coincident indicator of economic activity rose to 179.8, its highest level since it was created in January 1993, and sharply up on June's 168.8. The previous high was 168.9 last October.

The jump appeared to indicate that Lebanon may be emerging from 12-month slowdown in the rate of economic growth that began late last year and was accentuated by Israel's 17-day blitz on the country in April.

"The rise is mainly due to a pick up in construction," the Bank said. Increased construction -- the cornerstone of the economy -- was measured by increased cement deliveries which rose to 395,465 tonnes in July from 355,000 in June.

The indicator, which takes January 1993 as 100, combines 12 economic series including imports, exports, electricity output and airport and port activity. The Bank created it because of a lack of reliable data for calculating Gross Domestic Product (GDP).

Lebanon also registered its biggest monthly balance of payments surplus in 12 months at $142 million, bringing the accumulated surplus for the first seven months of 1996 to $180.5 million, the Bank said.
This compared with a $246.9 million deficit for the same period in 1995.
The accumulated balance of trade deficit for the year to date showed a slight improvement to $3.594 billion compared with $3.725 billion for the same period of 1995.
This was due to a slight decline in imports to $4.151 billion from $4.159 billion and a 28.8 percent increase in exports to $556.6 million from $434.9 million.
